chunks: He عليه السلام was asked about a group of people who had springs in land close to one another. One man wanted to make his spring lower than its original place, and some springs, when that is done to them, harm the others, while some do not cause harm because of the firmness of the land.
So he عليه السلام said: Whatever is in a hard, firm place does not harm it, and whatever is in loose, level soil, then it does cause harm.

key_terms.أَسْفَلَ: lower than its previous level or position
key_terms.عُيُونٌ: water springs owned or used by people

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on lowering a spring if it may harm neighboring springs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about adjacent water springs and whether altering one spring is permissible when it may affect others. The ruling distinguishes between firm ground, where such alteration does not cause harm, and loose soil, where it does cause harm and thus has legal consequence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3421 - Imam (as) was asked about a group of people who had springs in a land, with some springs being close to others. One of the men wanted to lower the level of his spring from its original position, but some of the springs, if altered in this way, could harm the others, while some would not cause harm due to the firmness of the soil.
Imam (as) said: "Whatever is in a solid, firm ground does not cause harm, but whatever is in a loose, sandy soil will cause harm."
